name: Mohammad Mustafa
role: Prime Minister of the State of Palestine, head of the 19th government of the Palestinian Authority (رئيس الوزراء); Minister of Foreign Affairs and Expatriates from March 2024 to June 2025
party: Independent (no party membership); member of the PLO Executive Committee since 2022
bio: Mohammad Mustafa (محمد مصطفى), born in 1954 in Kafr Sur near Tulkarm, is a Palestinian economist who spent about fifteen years at the World Bank in Washington before becoming chief executive (2006–2013) and then chairman (2015–2024) of the Palestine Investment Fund and senior economic adviser to President Mahmoud Abbas. He was Deputy Prime Minister for economic affairs from 2013 and Minister of National Economy until March 2015, when he resigned while in charge of Gaza's reconstruction after the 2014 war, and he joined the PLO Executive Committee as an independent in 2022. Abbas appointed him Prime Minister on 14 March 2024, under US and international pressure to 'revitalise' the Palestinian Authority; he and his 'technocratic' 19th government were sworn in on 31 March 2024, with Mustafa also holding the foreign affairs portfolio until a reshuffle on 23 June 2025. Hamas and other factions called his designation unilateral and without national consensus. His government's mandate centred on Gaza relief and reconstruction, reunifying Palestinian institutions and an internationally monitored reform agenda, including the 2025 reform of payments to prisoners and families of those killed in the conflict, whose implementation the United States and Israel dispute; it has faced what The Times of Israel called the PA's most severe financial crisis, after Israel's finance minister stopped transferring the clearance revenues Israel collects for the PA in 2025, leaving public employees on partial, delayed salaries. As of 22 October 2026 he remains Prime Minister and also heads the PA's liaison office with the Board of Peace's High Representative for Gaza, while day-to-day administration of Gaza under the US-backed plan was assigned to a technocratic committee that does not include the PA.
